steps.title: Prepare workspace and label tubes
steps.instruction: Choose and locate samples (box year, number, slot). Fill two containers with dry ice – one for tools (step 4) and one for tissue samples. Wipe cutting board, razor, and forceps with 70 % ethanol (avoid RNase‑away on dry‑ice contacts). Discard the razor in a sharps container. For each sample set aside: one green‑capped lysing tube with beads, three 1.5 ml tubes, one spin cartridge with collection tube, and one empty collection tube. Label all tubes clearly.

steps.title: Prepare DNase (if required)
steps.instruction: Resuspend DNase in 550 µl RNase‑free water (provided). Keep on ice.

steps.title: Record sample metadata and tissue amount
steps.instruction: Note specimen ID, animal ID, genotype, age, sex, and quantity of tissue. If tissue amount is low, cutting the tissue is not needed.

steps.title: Make DNase master mix per sample
steps.instruction: For each sample combine 8.0 µl 10× DNase I reaction buffer, 10.0 µl resuspended DNase, and 62.0 µl RNase‑free water (total 80 µl). Mix gently.

steps.title: Retrieve TRIzol and add to lysing tubes
steps.instruction: In a fume hood, take TRIzol™ from the 4 °C refrigerator. Pipette 1000 µl TRIzol into each lysing tube. If tissue has already been cut, add it to the tube and invert to mix. Optional: store tubes in TRIzol at –80 °C before homogenizing if you wish to pause the protocol.

steps.title: Cool lysing tubes during homogenization
steps.instruction: Replace the dry ice in the first container with wet ice (optional) or keep lysing tubes on wet ice or in a cold room for 2 min between homogenization runs to prevent RNA degradation from heat.

steps.title: Incubate lysate with TRIzol
steps.instruction: Incubate the lysate at room temperature for 5 min, ensuring all tissue is immersed in TRIzol.

steps.title: Homogenize tissue
steps.instruction: Select the appropriate tissue program (typically 40 s). Homogenize until the tissue appears as a fine powder in the TRIzol. For brain regions one 40‑second run is usually sufficient; larger organs may need three runs. Pink foam may appear after brain homogenization – it will disappear after a few minutes.

steps.title: Add chloroform and mix
steps.instruction: In a new 1.5 ml tube add 200 µl chloroform. Transfer 1000 µl lysate (TRIzol + tissue) into the same tube (do NOT add chloroform to the lysing tube). Gently invert 15–30 s to mix. Incubate at room temperature for 2–3 min.

steps.title: Centrifuge for phase separation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 4 °C, 12 000 × g for 15 min.

steps.title: Collect aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Transfer 400 µl of the upper (colorless) aqueous phase to a new 1.5 ml tube. Use two 200 µl transfers with a P200 pipette. If tissue or cell quantity is low, you may transfer 500 µl (tissues) or 600 µl (cells) to increase RNA concentration.

steps.title: Add ethanol and load spin cartridge
steps.instruction: Add 400–600 µl 70 % ethanol to the aqueous phase (RNA : ethanol = 1:1). Mix by pipetting up‑and‑down 4–5 times until RNA is no longer visible. Transfer 500 µl of this mixture to a spin cartridge placed in a collection tube.

steps.title: Wash cartridge with buffer II
steps.instruction: Add 500 µl Wash Buffer II to the spin cartridge. Centrifuge at room temperature, 12 000 × g for 20 s. Discard flow‑through and the collection tube, then insert the cartridge into a new collection tube.

steps.title: Optional on‑cartridge DNase treatment
steps.instruction: If DNase treatment is desired, perform the following three times:

substeps.instruction: Add 350 µl Wash Buffer I, centrifuge 12 000 × g 20 s, discard flow‑through and collection tube, insert cartridge into a new collection tube.
Add 80 µl PureLink DNase mixture to the cartridge center, incubate at room temperature for 15 min.
Repeat the Wash Buffer I step once more before proceeding to the next wash.

steps.title: Wash cartridge with buffer I
steps.instruction: Add 700 µl Wash Buffer I to the spin cartridge. Centrifuge at room temperature, 12 000 × g for 20 s. Discard flow‑through and collection tube, then insert the cartridge into a new 1.5 ml tube.

steps.title: Dry cartridge before elution
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at room temperature, 12 000 × g for 1 min to dry the spin cartridge.

steps.title: First elution with RNase‑free water
steps.instruction: Add 30 µl RNase‑free water to the cartridge center, incubate at room temperature for 30 s, then centrifuge at 12 000 × g for 2 min (if DNase was used, spin for 1 min). Collect the eluate.

steps.title: Second elution (20 µl water)
steps.instruction: Add 20 µl RNase‑free water to the cartridge, incubate 30 s, add the previously collected eluate (20 µl) to the cartridge center, incubate another 30 s, insert cartridge into a new 1.5 ml tube, and centrifuge at 12 000 × g for 2 min. Store the eluate on wet ice or at –80 °C.

steps.title: Third elution (optional 10 µl)
steps.instruction: Add 10 µl RNase‑free water to the cartridge and centrifuge at 12 000 × g for 2 min. Collect the eluate.

steps.title: Column‑free precipitation (if chosen)
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 ml isopropanol per 1 ml TRIzol used to the aqueous phase, mix, then continue with the ethanol‑wash steps described above.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in ethanol (cell samples)
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 ml 75 % ethanol per 1 ml TRIzol used. Centrifuge at 4 °C, 7 500 × g for 5 min. RNA can be stored in 75 % ethanol at –20 °C for up to 1 year or at 4 °C for up to 1 week.

steps.title: Air‑dry RNA pellet
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the RNA pellet for ~30 min at room temperature (or 1–2 min in a vacuum centrifuge). The goal is to evaporate residual ethanol, not water.

steps.title: Resuspend RNA and heat
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried pellet in 20–50 µl RNase‑free water by pipetting up‑and‑down. Incubate in a heat block at 55–60 °C for 10–15 min.

steps.title: Final storage
steps.instruction: Store the purified RNA at –70 °C (or –80 °C) or proceed directly to downstream applications.
